facts.text: KinesisMotor is the Thorlabs motor controller class; it implements FTDI chip connectivity via pyft232 (virtual serial interface)
The physical units are encoder steps for position (ratio to m or degrees depends on the connected stage), steps/sec for velocity, and steps/sec^2 for acceleration
get_position(scale=False) returns the position in the device internal units (steps)
move_to(position, scale=False) sends MOT_MOVE_TO (0x0453) with the position as a 32-bit signed integer
stop(immediate=True, sync=False) sends MOT_STOP (0x0465) with parameter 1 (abrupt stop); immediate=False sends parameter 2
is_moving is true when any of moving_fw, moving_bk, jogging_fw, jogging_bk or active is set
home(sync=False) sends MOT_HOME (0x0443); is_homing and is_homed read the homing and homed status bits
get_status returns the status strings of the status_bits table, which names the hardware and software limit switches, the motion bits, homing, interlock, overtemperature and error
get_velocity_parameters(scale=False) returns (min_velocity, acceleration, max_velocity) in device internal units; according to the documentation the minimal velocity is always zero
setup_velocity(max_velocity=..., scale=False) writes the velocity parameters and uses the current values for the ones given as None
get_device_info returns (serial_no, model_no, fw_ver, hw_type, hw_ver, mod_state, nchannels, notes) and get_number_of_channels returns nchannels
get_scale_units reports the scale units in use (deg, m, step, user_step, user or internal); this driver asks every value with scale=False and so always works in device internal units
